items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: Jerry was one of my teachers in college. ... I took private lessons with him at NEC.

ctx.x: Yes. You were sort of facing the drummer. You weren’t addressing the audience. It’s almost like — I assumed it was like one of those things, “Okay here’s what we’re going to do, you play the first eight, I’ll do —” you know like you were doing an instant arrangement.

Yeah, yeah. We were playing up in Portsmouth at a place called the Press Room. We’ve done a few concerts, Jerry and I. Jerry was one of my teachers in college. One of the great artists of our time, one of the greatest tenor players ever. Great educator too. You know I took private lessons with him at NEC. Yeah I think at that moment we were either — for those gigs we didn’t have a set list, so we were either talking about how the tune we were playing was going to go or what we were going to play next. And yeah,…
And then it happened. And then it sounded like it was, just like it was supposed to be.
